jobs.description: Employer: General Motors Expires: 10/22/2026 Job DescriptionAbout Digital Products Digital Products owns the definition, development, and delivery of GM’s digital products and the customer experiences delivered through mobile applications, back-office platforms, and connected services. The organization brings together OnStar & Customer Experience Platforms and Digital Vehicle Experience and works closely with Vehicle Products to deliver digital contributors to the vehicle experience. Digital Products is an exciting place to begin your career because interns can work on real products, services, tools, and experiences that connect customers with GM. You will learn from experienced professionals, collaborate across product and engineering teams, and gain exposure to how digital products are built, tested, launched, and improved. Depending on the team, you may contribute to application development, automation, data and integration services, software delivery, test tools, or lab and validation infrastructure. Assignments are connected to real team priorities and may include design, coding, testing, troubleshooting, documentation, and continuous improvement across the development lifecycle. Potential Team & Areas of Work Opportunities may be aligned to the following groups and product areas from the Digital Products intern intake: Consumer Digital Experiences (CDE): Mobile, Vehicle Contact Centers & OnStar Safety, and OnStar AI Engineering Physical and Virtual Test Platforms: Virtual Test Infrastructure, Virtualization Tools, Vehicle Reflash, Infotainment Lab Operations, HIL simulation integration, and lab operations Vehicle Software Integrity and Delivery: Calibration Management Tools, Greylock, Wired Programming, and VCAM Digital Vehicle Experience (DVE): Software engineering and software test opportunities supporting digital vehicle experiences Potential Skills & ContributionsBuild or enhance software features, services, APIs, tools, or automation Write unit, integration, or end-to-end tests and help improve software quality Analyze data, investigate defects, and support troubleshooting or root-cause analysis Contribute to technical designs, requirements, documentation, or delivery plans Support software delivery, diagnostics, reflash, validation, lab tooling, or test infrastructure Collaborate with engineers, product managers, designers, analysts, or related field.Must have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internshipAvailability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the 12 week clearly, work collaboratively, and learn new technologies Interest in building reliable, customer-focused digital products Ability to work onsite at the assigned GM location with the manager and team Preferred Experience Candidates are not expected to meet every qualification listed below. Experience with one or more programming languages such as Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C#, C++, or SQL Exposure to software testing, automation, APIs, databases, Git, CI/CD, observability, or integration tools Experience with mobile development, web development, backend services, data engineering, Salesforce, MuleSoft, or test platforms A class project, personal project, internship, portfolio, or code sample that demonstrates problem-solving Compensation: The monthly salary range for this role is $6,400-$10,300 per month. Why OpenGov?A Mission That Matters.At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Front-end skills with JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, or React (preferred). Foundational knowledge of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), data structures, and algorithms. Strong analytical, debugging, and communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote Agile/Scrum environment. Availability during Eastern Standard Time (EST) business hours. Prior internship, co-op, or relevant professional experience is a plus. This internship/co-op provides an opportunity to contribute to full-stack development projects, explore innovative technologies, and grow your technical expertise in a supportive, hands-on environment. If you're motivated, curious, and ready to learn, we'd love to talk to you! EducationThis role does not require a degree. jobs.title: Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Pieper Electric, Inc. - Pieper Electric, Inc Expires: 10/22/2026 Job DescriptionPosition Summary BIM is something we use. VDC is how we use digital information and technology to plan, coordinate, and improve how we build. As a Virtual Design & Construction Intern at Pieper Electric, you will learn how Building Information Modeling (BIM) supports the larger Virtual Design and Construction (VDC) process. You will gain hands-on experience using digital construction tools that support planning and field execution through model navigation, clash detection, constructability reviews, layout, and prefabrication. Working alongside BIM Specialists, Detailing Specialists, Project Managers, field leaders, and other project partners, you will help develop and coordinate constructible electrical models and drawings that connect design information to how work is planned, fabricated, laid out, and installed in the field. This internship is designed for students who enjoy technology, problem-solving, spatial thinking, and seeing how things are built. You do not need to know every BIM platform before joining us. We are looking for students who are curious, detail-oriented, willing to learn, and interested in understanding how digital models can be used to solve real construction challenges. Interns will receive guidance, feedback, and opportunities to take ownership of defined assignments under appropriate supervision. Values and Ways of Working At Pieper Electric, we believe in the Power to Serve and the Pursuit of Excellence. Our values, a Servant’s Heart, Wisdom, Integrity, Courage, Humility, and Passion, guide how we learn, collaborate, support the field, and serve our customers and teammates. As an intern, you will be encouraged to ask questions, share ideas, take initiative, and learn from experienced professionals while contributing to a safe and respectful team environment. Essential Responsibilities Safety and Field Engagement Complete required safety training and follow all company, customer, and jobsite requirements.Participate in supervised jobsite and prefabrication shop visits to understand how model information translates to installation.Learn how BIM supports safer planning, constructability, layout, prefabrication, and field execution.Promptly communicate safety concerns, field observations, or differences between modeled conditions and field conditions.BIM Modeling and Model Navigation Learn to navigate, review, create, and update 3D electrical models using Revit and other company BIM platforms.Assist with modeling electrical systems and components in support of coordination, constructability, prefabrication, layout, and installation.Review project drawings, specifications, submittals, and other available project information to support accurate model development.Update models as design information, coordination decisions, and field conditions change.Prepare model views and information that help project and field teams understand planned installation.Coordination, Clash Detection and Constructability Participate in BIM coordination and constructability reviews with project teams and trade partners.Learn how electrical systems are coordinated with architectural, structural, mechanical, plumbing, fire protection, and other building systems.Assist with identifying, documenting, and resolving clashes or spatial conflicts before installation.Review modeled routing and installation approaches with constructability, access, sequencing, and field execution in mind.Support approved model revisions resulting from coordination and constructability reviews.Detailing, Layout and Field Execution Assist with coordinated drawings, installation details, layouts, point drawings, and other field-ready information generated from or supported by BIM.Learn to interpret electrical symbols, one-lines, schedules, construction drawings, and model information.Support digital and model-based layout activities used to accurately locate electrical work in the field.Help prepare clear information for field teams and incorporate field feedback into models and drawings as directed.Prefabrication Support Learn how coordinated BIM content supports prefabrication and assembly planning.Assist with models, drawings, dimensions, material information, and documentation used to support prefabricated electrical assemblies.Participate in prefabrication shop visits to see how digital construction information becomes physical assemblies.Help maintain alignment between model information, prefabrication requirements, and planned field installation.Project Documentation and BIM Quality Maintain organized and accurate models, drawings, revisions, and project files.Perform assigned model and drawing quality checks for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.Support installation, record, and as-built documentation as directed.Follow company standards for file naming, version control, model organization, and documentation.Communication and Team Collaboration Collaborate with BIM, detailing, project management, prefabrication, field, and trade partners.Participate in team and coordination meetings and track assigned follow-up items.Ask questions when project requirements, design intent, or model information are unclear.Seek feedback, apply lessons learned, and communicate changes or potential delays to assigned work.Contribute ideas that improve BIM workflows, constructability, coordination, or the flow of information to the field.Learning and Continuous Improvement Participate in BIM software training, mentorship, and technical learning opportunities.Develop an understanding of how BIM fits within VDC and supports a project from preconstruction and coordination through prefabrication, installation, and closeout.Build familiarity with model navigation, clash detection, constructability reviews, layout, prefabrication, and other digital construction workflows.Explore career opportunities in BIM, detailing, VDC, and electrical construction.Complete a capstone or project assignment that provides a practical contribution to the team.

jobs.title: Hardware Test Engineering Co-Op at Delta Faucet Company
jobs.description: Employer: Delta Faucet Company - Delta Faucet HQ- Indianapolis, IN Expires: 10/23/2026 At Delta Faucet, we are committed to transforming everyday experiences with water through innovative products and exceptional service. As a leader in the plumbing industry, we take pride in our dedication to quality, sustainability, and customer satisfaction. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen our mission to create solutions that inspire and elevate the lives of all our customers. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds to join us on this journey toward inclusivity and excellence. Your Role at Delta FaucetDelta Faucet Company has an opportunity for a Hardware Engineering Co-op to join our Connected Water Team to help deliver the next generation of product features and technology to our customers. In this role, you will support the development of new digital products through hands-on work with embedded systems and real product hardware. You will spend most of your days in the lab doing hands-on and varied tasks: soldering and reworking assemblies, programming and bringing up circuit boards, running electrical and functional tests, laying out PCBs, and keeping our engineering lab and its equipment running as smoothly as possible.You will report to the engineering manager and sit with the project teams, not apart from them. Within your first few weeks you will be assigned specific tasks, projects, and test processes to own — meaning you make the calls there, you document how it works, and you are the person others ask about it. When you find a better way to do something, we want to hear it, and we will give you a straight answer either way. Every part of the role is scoped so that the skills you leave with — test methodology, debugging discipline, documentation, lab ownership — are the ones that help you with the rest of your college work and prepare you for your future career. Responsibilities:Build and ReworkSolder, rework, and modify through-hole and surface-mount assemblies for prototypes, test fixtures, and engineering samples.Assemble and wire test fixtures, harnesses, and benchtop setups from schematics and written instructions.Program, flash, and bring up circuit boards; verify power rails, signal integrity, and basic functionality on new builds.Test and DebugExecute electrical, functional, and reliability tests on products and subassemblies, and record results accurately.Investigate test failures: reproduce the issue, isolate it to a component or subsystem, and document what you found so an engineer can act on it.Write and maintain basic test scripts and data-logging routines to automate repetitive measurements.Operate and troubleshoot standard bench equipment — oscilloscopes, DMMs, power supplies, function generators, data acquisition systems, environmental chambers.Design SupportProduce PCB layouts for test fixtures, adapter boards, and design revisions under engineering guidance.Review schematics and layouts for manufacturability and testability, and raise concerns before boards are ordered.Suggest product and process improvements based on what you observe on the benchLab and Calibration OwnershipOrganize and manage the engineering lab: equipment inventory, tool and fixture storage, consumable stock, workspace layout, and bench readiness.Run the equipment calibration program — track calibration due dates, coordinate with vendors, maintain certificates, and keep instruments in a known-good state.Establish and document standard operating procedures for test setups, lab safety, and equipment use so results are repeatable across people and across time.Maintain clear technical documentation: test reports, procedures, wiring diagrams, bring-up notes, and change records.Where this goesWe treat this co-op as the first step in a career here, not a temporary set of hands. The scope is designed to grow with you:In your first term, you will learn our products, our lab, and our test methods, supporting engineers on defined tasks.As you demonstrate judgment, you will take ownership of specific test areas, fixtures, and the calibration program — work that is yours, with your name on it.Strong co-ops are invited back for additional terms with expanded responsibility, and we actively look to convert high performers into full-time engineering or test roles at graduation.You will finish with a portfolio of real work: products you helped validate, fixtures you designed, procedures you wrote, and failures you tracked down. That is experience that transfers anywhere — and we would rather you build it here and stay. QualificationsCurrently pursuing a Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, or related fieldDemonstrated hands-on experience — coursework labs, senior design, competition teams (IEEE, Robotics, etc.), maker projects, or personal builds. Show us what you have made.Excellent soldering experience, including small components and SMT reworkFoundational understanding of analog and digital circuits. Comfort reading schematics and interpreting datasheets and basic specifications.Careful, methodical work habits. In test engineering, sloppy data is worse than no data, and this role is built on trustworthy measurements.Clear written communication — you will write procedures and failure reports that other people rely on.Familiarity with microcontrollers, embedded systems, and electronics lab equipmentStrong problem-solving skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn in a hands-on engineering environmentInterest in IoT, connected products, or consumer electronics is a plus The target compensation for the role is $22.00 hour. Why Join Us?At Delta Faucet Company, our people are our greatest assets. We value different perspectives and fostering an inclusive environment. You’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our brand, working alongside passionate professionals committed to excellence and innovation. Join us to lead progressive growth and make a significant impact within a leading organization.Here are some of the benefits we offer for your personal and professional growth:Culture: Recognized and award-winning reputation for equality, diversity and inclusion, flexibility, work-life balance, and more.Wellbeing: Comprehensive benefit plans; retirement, savings, tuition reimbursement, and employee incentive programs; resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.Learning & Development: LinkedIn Learning access; internal opportunities to work on projects cross-company.Social Impact: Four employee-led and self-directed Business Resource Groups; Paid volunteer day annually; Employees share their time, skills and talent with charities and nonprofit organizations across the U.S. and around the globe. jobs.title: Synchronization Planning Co-Op at Colgate-Palmolive
jobs.description: Employer: Colgate-Palmolive Expires: 10/23/2026 Position OverviewThe Synchronization Planning Co-Op plays a vital role within the Synchronization Planning Team supporting End-to-End (E2E) supply and demand synchronization processes. This position is designed for a university student to work throughout the academic year and summer. In this role, you will leverage advanced analytics, data engineering, and automation tools to optimize planning solutions, enhance organizational visibility, and streamline workflows. You will work directly with the various planning teams on E2E planning process improvements, automated presentation building, master data governance, and predictive analytics projects. Key ResponsibilitiesAutomation & Optimization: Build, automate, and maintain planning workflows and optimization solutions using Google Apps Script, SQL queries in Snowflake, and Python. Analytics & Visualization: Design, build, and maintain interactive business intelligence dashboards in Sigma and DOMO to track key E2E planning metrics and trends. AI Solutions & Workflows: Explore and implement AI assistants and custom automation solutions utilizing Google Workspace tools to streamline daily planning operational tasks. E2E Planning Projects: Partner directly with the manager to lead and execute process improvement projects, including fill rate root cause analysis, fill rate projections, inventory projections, and ad-hoc E2E initiatives. Meeting & Presentation Automation: Prepare content and automate slide generation for ongoing synchronization meetings to improve reporting efficiency and accuracy. Master Data Governance: Perform scheduled (monthly/quarterly) master data audit checks, identify discrepancies, and recommend data quality corrections in core systems such as SAP and Kinaxis. Documentation & Standards: Help organize, update, and standardize End-to-End process documentation and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a Bachelor’s or Master's degree program in Supply Chain Management, Data Analytics, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Ability to commit to a year-round Co-Op schedule (September 2026 – August 2027), balancing full-time/part-time hours alongside university coursework. Intermediate to advanced proficiency in writing SQL queries (Snowflake preferred). Foundational experience or strong proficiency in Python for data manipulation/optimization and Google Apps Script for task automation. Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively in team settings. Preferred QualificationsExperience creating data visualizations and dashboards in Sigma, DOMO, or similar BI tools. Hands-on experience with Google Suite automation, Google Cloud Platform, or Google Workspace AI tools. Familiarity with Supply Planning, Production Planning, Inventory Management, or SAP S/4HANA systems. Passion for continuous process improvement, problem-solving, and data governance. jobs.title: Video Editor Intern at Dancephreakz
jobs.description: Employer: Dancephreakz Expires: 10/23/2026 Phrkz Network | DancePhreakzLocation: Los Angeles County, CA | HybridPosition Type: Part-Time InternshipSchedule: Approximately 8–15 hours per weekCompensation: Paid InternshipAbout the Organization:DancePhreakz is a dynamic, women-owned, and BIPOC-led dance and entertainment production company that is revolutionizing the industry. We bring creativity, energy, and authenticity to the world of dance and movement. Through our four divisions—Production, Apparel, Academy, and our newly acquired studio and event space—we aim to build a platform where BIPOC movement artists thrive, fostering a community that is unapologetically fierce, creative, and ready to make an impact.About Phrkz NetworkPhrkz Network is a new media and entertainment division of DancePhreakz launching in 2026. The Network is an evolution of DancePhreakz's production work into a dedicated home for original shows, podcasts, interviews, digital series, visual projects, documentaries, and culture-driven entertainment.As we build the Network, we're looking for emerging editors who want hands-on experience helping shape the look, pace, and storytelling style of an original digital entertainment platform.About the InternshipWe're seeking two Video Editor & Post-Production Interns to join our growing production team.This is an editing-first position for creatives who already have hands-on editing experience and want to strengthen their portfolio while working on real entertainment programming.You'll edit both long-form and short-form content, including full-length video podcasts, original shows, multi-camera productions, interviews, trailers, teasers, YouTube content, Reels, TikToks, and YouTube Shorts.We want editors who understand that great editing isn't simply cutting footage together. It's about finding the story, creating a hook, controlling pacing, capturing personality, and making viewers want to keep watching.Our creative inspiration comes from modern digital entertainment and culture-driven media platforms such as Hoorae Media, Keytv, Complex, The Black Effect, SpringHill, REVOLT, Joe Budden Podcast, and similar creator-led networks. We're looking for editors interested in understanding what makes their content feel current, entertaining, polished, and highly shareable.What You'll DoLong-Form & Podcast EditingEdit full-length video podcasts, interviews, original shows, and digital series for YouTube and other platforms. Edit multi-camera productions and seamlessly switch between angles based on conversation, reactions, and story. Sync and edit multiple camera and audio sources. Edit and prepare audio versions of podcast episodes for Spotify, Apple Podcasts, and other podcast platforms. Perform color correction, dialogue cleanup, audio balancing, and basic sound design. Add intros/outros, lower thirds, graphics, captions, music, B-roll, and branded elements. Create engaging openings and maintain strong pacing throughout longer episodes. Short-Form & Promotional EditingTurn long-form episodes into compelling Reels, TikToks, and YouTube Shorts. Identify moments with strong hooks, reactions, humor, controversy, insight, or emotional impact. Create trailers, teasers, cold opens, episode promos, and highlight packages. Reframe and optimize content for vertical and horizontal formats. Understand that a 60-second social edit requires different pacing and storytelling than a 45-minute YouTube episode. Post-Production WorkflowOrganize raw footage, project files, audio, graphics, and final exports. Maintain organized editing projects that another editor can easily open and understand. Complete revisions based on producer/director notes. Export content according to platform specifications. Help maintain consistent editing and visual standards across Phrkz Network programming. Manage multiple assignments while meeting production deadlines.QualificationsMust reside in Los Angeles County, California.Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a college/university program in film, media, communications, or a related field—or equivalent experience/portfolio.Previous video editing experience is required—this is not a learn-from-zero editing internship.Portfolio, demo reel, or work samples required.Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, AVID, or comparable professional editing software.Experience editing both short-form and/or long-form content.Strong understanding of storytelling, pacing, music, sound, reactions, and visual rhythm.Comfortable working with multi-camera footage.Basic knowledge of audio editing, color correction, captions, graphics, and exporting.Able to work independently and make creative decisions without requiring detailed instructions for every cut.Strong time management and ability to work within quick turnaround deadlines.Comfortable receiving notes, making revisions, and collaborating with producers and other editors.Interest in entertainment, pop culture, podcasts, music, dance, digital media, and original programming.Internship DetailsSchedule: 8–15 hours per week with flexible scheduling to accommodate classes or other commitments.Location: Hybrid—remote editing plus occasional on-site filming in Gardena, CA.Compensation: Paid internshipAcademic credit available if approved by your institution.Other Information:Exempt/Non-Exempt: ExemptEOE Statement: We are an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 10/24/2026 The Laboratory for Physical Sciences (LPS) Advanced Computing Systems (ACS) team in the NSA Research Directorate is joining its counterparts in the Capabilities and Operations Directorates to provide a select number of undergraduate students with an exciting 10-week summer internship at LPS, located in the Research Park building complex adjacent to the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). The Future Computing Summer Internship (FCSI) program was established in 2022 to expose participants to High-Performance Computing (HPC), a field critical to national security, discovery, and technological innovation. FCSI is intended for undergraduate students who will complete their junior year by Spring 2027 and are pursuing degrees in Mathematics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Artificial Intelligence. These students possess strong mathematical and computer programming foundations and technical skills relevant to HPC. Participants do not enter an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD, or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Applicants who have only assisted on set should consider if they are ready to lead a complete production independently.Working knowledge of camera operation, audio recording, and basic studio and field lighting.Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro or similar non-linear editing softwareReliable and composed under tight deadlines and fast-paced workflows.Collaborative, receptive to direction and feedback, and able to communicate clearly with producers and on-camera talent.Professionalism, reliability, and attention to detail — production work demands technical precision, consistent follow-through, and professional conduct on set.Preferred QualificationsExperience in live broadcast production, including operating production switchers or managing multi-camera workflows.Knowledge of studio lighting arrangements and broadcast camera equipment.Experience directing or producing documentary or long-form nonfiction content.FAA drone pilot certification or experience in aerial cinematography.A production portfolio showcasing versatility across formats — studio, field, short-form, and long-form.Finalists will be asked to share a production portfolio or video editing sample.The Cato Internship ProgramCato’s paid internships are available for undergraduates, recent graduates, graduate students, law students, and early-career professionals who are strongly committed to individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace—principles that together form libertarianism, also known as “classical liberalism,” “market liberalism,” or, to many of our international friends, simply “liberalism.” All Cato interns participate in the same intensive seminar series, which covers a wide range of topics in history, philosophy, policy, and professional development. Interns also assist with events and occasionally support Cato staff with other daily tasks. Interns receive competitive pay. Part-time roles are adjusted accordingly and require a minimum of 25 hours per week. Program participants must be able to attend in person in Washington, D.C. For more information about the internship program and experience, we encourage you to explore our website. If you have any questions, email studentprograms@cato.org.
